reviewers.summary: The latest change wires the guide-line adapter into App’s production 3D scene and adds production-path tests for route confirmation and arrival. I found no remaining in-scope defect from the previous round.

The production scene now mounts the guide-line adapter, but its reduced-motion control and arrival selection path are not connected to production behavior. The confirmation test also does not verify the required mapped destination.

findingList.message: Pass the App's reduced-motion state to the production guide-line adapter. The production control currently does not affect whether the confirmed route is static.

evidence.codePathTraced: The production adapter is rendered without a reducedMotion prop, while the existing App controls update hangarReducedMotion. The adapter therefore uses its system-preference fallback instead of the App setting.
evidence.failureScenario: When the system preference is not reduced and a user enables reduced motion through the App control, confirming a rack entry still renders an animated guide line instead of the required static line.

findingList.message: Arrival is wired only to an optional injected callback, not the shared production aircraft-selection handler required by the criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The production selection callback only calls the optional hangarAircraftSelectionHandler prop. App does not provide a default handler or connect this callback to the scene's pointer and keyboard selection path.
evidence.failureScenario: When the normal App is rendered without the optional prop, a user can confirm an entry and walk to its marker, but arrival calls a no-op and does not select the aircraft through the shared production handler.

findingList.message: The named production confirmation test does not assert that the route ends at AIR-1's expected marker `{x:4,z:-4}`, so a broken marker mapping passes.

evidence.codePathTraced: The production confirmation test checks only that a polyline exists; it never checks the polyline points or another exact value identifying AIR-1's mapped marker.
evidence.failureScenario: If AIR-1 is mapped to the wrong marker, the test still passes because the production scene renders some route polyline.

reviewers.summary: The changed production wiring and tests introduce no reachable injection, authorization, credential exposure, path traversal, or unsafe deserialization vulnerability. The adapter uses React rendering and the route flow makes no network calls.
